tagline: Cattle country, cypress water and the opening of a long war.
intro: The byway runs 62 miles of country road through Sumter County, by way of Rutland near the Withlacoochee, Lake Panasoffkee, Sumterville, Bushnell, Webster and Linden, past cattle ranches, horse farms and hardwood forest.

A 1925 number of Travelon Magazine called the county the storehouse of Florida, a place where good living could be made on ten acres of land. Before the farms, Seminoles held councils by Lake Panasoffkee, and the Second Seminole War began in this county.

moments.title: Rutland
moments.text: Rutland sits between the cypress-lined Withlacoochee and Lake Panasoffkee and lives on farming and recreation, an airboat tour company included.

moments.title: Lake Panasoffkee
moments.text: Black Seminoles settled by the lake about 1813 and raised corn, rice and sugar cane, and after the battle of Wahoo Swamp Osceola, possibly ill with malaria, came here to live among them.

moments.title: Dade Battlefield
moments.text: On December 28, 1835, Seminole warriors and Black Seminole allies ambushed Major Dade's column on the Fort King Road here, and of more than 100 soldiers only three survived.
